g.text: OpSIS recently shut down — the book gives two reasons:

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 8.5px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #f6f6f6

g.text: 1 no pre-existing commercial process to leverage

text.style: font-size: 8px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #f6f6f6

g.text: commercial users were “rightly unwilling to rely on

text.style: font-size: 8px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #f6f6f6
font-weight: 700; font-size: 8.5px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #f6f6f6
font-size: 8px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #f6f6f6

g.text: money from research users and funders could not

text.style: font-size: 8px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #f6f6f6

g.text: keep it going or develop commercial-grade processes

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 8.8px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #f6f6f6

g.text: Takeaway: the fabs and wafers exist, and MPW services open them to academics, students and industry —

text.style: font-size: 8.8px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #f6f6f6

g.text: but every open process is prototyping-only (tiny volumes) — a significant impediment for OpSIS, which also lacked funding.
